title: Another Paragon spinout goes public through reverse merger
content: An article from Another Paragon spinout goes public through reverse merger Including the deal announced Tuesday, Paragon has now formed and taken eight startups public through reverse mergers. The ninth sold for $11 billion. Published Oct. 13, 2026 Jacob Bell Lead Reporter Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Velaris Therapeutics is the latest in a series of biotech startups Paragon Labs has formed and subsequently taken public. Getty Images Paragon Labs, the biotechnology incubator behind more than half a dozen startups, watched another of its companies go public Tuesday through an increasingly popular type of deal. Velaris Therapeutics is the ninth and newest spinout from Paragon, with research directed at diseases of the heart and lungs. It’s just been acquired by Alaunos Therapeutics, a former cell therapy developer that abandoned its programs in 2023 and has since been looking for a lifeline in a strategic deal. if (!$(selector).closest('.pf-comments__ad-wrapper').hasClass('borders')) { $(selector).closest('.pf-comments__ad-wrapper').addClass('borders') } } }); } }); }); While branded an acquisition, the deal’s terms are more aligned with a “reverse merger,” where a private company slots into a public “shell” and takes control of the operations. The combined business will focus on Velaris’ drug programs, and four of its five board directors will be either from or picked by Fairmount Funds, the Philadelphia-based investment firm that founded Paragon in 2021. Alongside the deal, Fairmount led a private stock offering that raised around $350 million to support Velaris’ research and keep the new company operational into 2029. Several other big-name investors participated in the round, including Venrock Healthcare Capital Partners, Wellington Management, Janus Henderson Investors, Perceptive Advisors and certain accounts advised by T. Rowe Price Investment Management. “We believe this transaction and the concurrent private placement provide a strong financial foundation for us to advance an exciting pipeline and offer our stockholders a compelling opportunity to realize value,” Holger Weis, CEO and board chairman at Alaunos, said in a statement. Until recently, many healthcare investors viewed reverse mergers as unsavory deals between a washed-out public company and a private drugmaker whose assets weren’t interesting enough to drive an initial public offering. But that image has changed drastically over the last couple years. That’s largely because of Fairmount, which showed these deals, when backed by tight groups of credible investors, can offer promising private developers a fast track to the public markets. if (window.dfp_visibility === 'mobile' ) { googletag.cmd.push(function() { googletag.defineSlot( '/3618/biopharmadive/biopharmadivehybrid2', [[300, 250], 'fluid'], 'dfp-hybrid2-mobile' ).addService(googletag.pubads()); }); } waitToLoadAds.push(function() { googletag.cmd.push(function() { if (window.dfp_visibility === 'mobile' ) { window.onDvtagReady?.(() => googletag.display('dfp-hybrid2-mobile')); googletag.pubads().addEventListener('slotRenderEnded', function (event) { var adUnitPath = '/3618/biopharmadive/biopharmadivehybrid2'; var onProformative = false; if (onProformative && event.slot.getAdUnitPath() === adUnitPath && !event.isEmpty ) { var adUnitPathWithVisibility = adUnitPath + '-mobile'; var selector = '.pf-comments__ad-wrapper #dfp-hybrid2-mobile'; if (!$(selector).closest('.pf-comments__ad-wrapper').hasClass('borders')) { $(selector).closest('.pf-comments__ad-wrapper').addClass('borders') } } }); } }); }); More than two dozen biotech reverse mergers have been announced this year — a marked increase from the 10 seen across all of 2025 — according to a database compiled by life sciences advisory firm JB Strategy Partners. That figure roughly matches the total number of IPOs so far in 2026. In addition to Velaris, this new class has two other Paragon-forged companies: the migraine specialist Mentari Therapeutics and the brain drug developer Korsana Biosciences. Each came with private stock offerings worth hundreds of millions of dollars. Mentari’s deal is set to close before the end of the year. If it does, eight of Paragon’s nine disclosed spinouts will have gone public through reverse mergers. The lone exception is Apogee Therapeutics, an immunology-focused biotech that raised $300 million through an IPO in 2023. Apogee then sold to AbbVie in a nearly $11 billion deal that closed last month. Branden Berns, a partner at the law firm Gibson Dunn who helped advise Velaris, explained to BioPharma Dive that, generally, private companies exploring reverse mergers have the bandwidth to evaluate around two to five public vehicles. That was the case with Velaris. The companies also did a speedier, often harder-to-pull-off version known as a simultaneous sign and close. At least two other Paragon biotechs, Spyre Therapeutics and Damora Therapeutics, used the same approach. "The Fairmount team is very capable at identifying appropriate counterparties and executing transactions quickly,” Berns said. The combined company said that, along with Velaris' pipeline, it does intend to keep working on an obesity and metabolic disorders drug that Alaunos pivoted to after stepping back from cancer cell therapies. title: 誉衡药业1115万元受让首都医科大学专利，加码TLK2靶向基因治疗，开辟青光眼视神经保护新路径
content: 首页 资讯 摩熵原创 时讯 誉衡药业1115万元受让首都医科大学专利，加码TLK2靶向基因治疗，开辟青光眼视神经保护新路径 誉衡药业1115万元受让首都医科大学专利，加码TLK2靶向基因治疗，开辟青光眼视神经保护新路径 李明轩 · 医药投融资分析师 李 李明轩 医药投融资分析师 审核：孙浩 · 特许金融分析师（CFA） 聚焦创新药投融资、小核酸药物与代谢疾病赛道；长期跟踪国内 Biotech 融资动态与管线进展。累计发布原创分析 200+ 篇。 14小时前 952 哈尔滨誉衡药业股份有限公司 首都医科大学 TLK2 青光眼 基因治疗 10月16日，哈尔滨誉衡药业发布公告，公司与首都医科大学签署专利权转让合同，以1115万元受让发明专利 “一种钙超载介导神经元死亡的标志物及应用”（专利号：ZL202210351580.3）。图源：誉衡药业企业公告本次交易瞄准青光眼神经保护赛道，基于该专利技术，誉衡药业计划开发靶向 TLK2 的基因治疗疗法，为青光眼治疗开辟独立于降眼压之外的全新研发方向。一、青光眼治疗：瞄准神经保护新路径青光眼被称作 “视力小偷”，是全球首位不可逆性致盲眼病。根据《中国青光眼指南（2020 年）》数据，2020年国内青光眼患者约2100万人，致盲人数高达567万人；随着人口老龄化，我国青光眼的患病率将逐年增加。当前临床主流治疗方案，核心思路集中于降低眼压。但临床痛点十分突出：部分患者即便眼压控制达标，视神经损伤依旧会持续恶化。视网膜神经节细胞（RGC）进行性凋亡，才是青光眼视功能不可逆丧失的核心病理根源。誉衡本次收购专利，正是瞄准这一临床痛点。专利围绕钙超载介导神经元死亡机制，计划开发TLK2靶向基因疗法，探索不依赖降眼压、直接保护视网膜神经节细胞的治疗路径。从作用机制来看，该项目和现有多数神经保护研发路线存在明显差异，具备机制创新潜力。但需要客观说明：技术仍处于早期阶段，疗效、安全性以及商业化价值，仍有待漫长的研发进程验证。二、1115 万元分期支付，后续研发仍待推进按照转让合同约定：首都医科大学需要在合同生效后30个工作日内，向誉衡药业完整移交技术秘密、专利使用资料、技术背景文件与可行性研究报告等全套技术材料；誉衡药业则在同期完成专利权转让登记手续。1115万元转让款并非一次性支付，将按照研发里程碑节点分期拨付。高校基础成果向临床药物转化，本身充满不确定性。本次专利交易落地，只是项目的起点。后续候选疗法的开发、临床前验证、临床试验推进，才是决定这项专利价值能否兑现的关键。三、青光眼基因治疗赛道升温，国内外多条路线同台竞速不止TLK2靶点技术，青光眼基因治疗领域早已进入多点布局阶段，研发方向分化为致病基因编辑、房水流出调控、视神经保护三大主线。·国内管线本导基因BD113：针对MYOC突变型青光眼，采用基因编辑敲除致病变异基因，已于北京同仁医院完成2例患者给药。艾威药业GVB-2001：抑制Rho通路改善房水外流，面向原发性开角型青光眼，摩熵医药数据库显示，该药在2025年7月进入Ⅱ期临床阶段。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库极目生物ARVN601：基于微小RNA的神经保护基因疗法，目前处于临床前研发阶段。·海外管线Life Biosciences ER-100：表观遗传重编程技术，AAV载体递送山中因子，布局开角型青光眼与缺血性视神经病变，2026年完成Ⅰ期临床首例给药。安斯泰来ASP2767：聚焦青光眼视神经损伤修复，采用单次玻璃体腔注射给药方案。不难看出，青光眼研发范式正在迭代：从单纯降眼压的对症治疗，转向深层致病机制干预、视神经保护的对因治疗。誉衡药业1115万元拿下TLK2相关专利，是企业布局眼科创新赛道的重要动作。这项具备差异化机制的技术，后续研发推进值得行业持续关注。参考来源：[1] title: In the hunt for reverse merger targets, Caribou could be prized game
content: An article from Emerging biotech In the hunt for reverse merger targets, Caribou could be prized game The struggling cell therapy developer is exploring strategic alternatives, which, among other characteristics, make it a likely candidate to receive reverse merger interest. Published Oct. 8, 2026 Jacob Bell Lead Reporter Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Getty Images On Wall Street, a major search is underway to find struggling public companies that can serve as the raw materials for a niche but booming business. A promising candidate may have just emerged. This business revolves around “reverse mergers,” a type of deal where a private company combines with a public counterpart, often as a quick way to access the broad and deep-pocketed array of investors found on marketplaces like the Nasdaq. While previously disparaged, reverse mergers have recently become so popular that some deal experts question whether there are enough quality “shell” companies to meet the demand. if (window.dfp_visibility === 'mobile' ) { googletag.cmd.push(function() { googletag.defineSlot( '/3618/biopharmadive/biopharmadivehybrid1', [[300, 250], 'fluid'], 'dfp-hybrid1-mobile' ).addService(googletag.pubads()); if (!$(selector).closest('.pf-comments__ad-wrapper').hasClass('borders')) { $(selector).closest('.pf-comments__ad-wrapper').addClass('borders') } } }); } }); }); Shell hunters could have another option following a Tuesday announcement from Caribou Biosciences, the once high-flying biotechnology startup co-founded by CRISPR gene editing pioneer Jennifer Doudna. In a statement, Caribou CEO Rachel Haurwitz said the current financing environment has made it “increasingly challenging” to secure the money needed to advance the company’s two main research programs, which focus on a hard-to-make form of medicine known as “off-the-shelf” cell therapy. As such, Caribou has made the “difficult decision” not to further develop its programs and to “evaluate strategic alternatives” — common corporate lingo for opening itself up to various deals. Caribou’s board of directors has already cleared management to start evaluating a potential merger, acquisition, business combination or other transactions. The company has also tapped Wedbush Securities to serve as its exclusive financial advisor in this process. To Daina Graybosch, an analyst at Leerink Partners who covers Caribou, the natural end for the company now is either a reverse merger or an acquisition by Tang Capital, a San Diego-based investment firm that made a name for itself by buying up cash-rich biotechs and returning much of their value to shareholders. Caribou ended the second quarter with $114 million worth of cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities. “I think Rachel and the team really do believe in their assets, but it's a real struggle,” Graybosch said. “And when you finally do raise [capital], it just gets more and more dilutive. To pull the trigger now and give money back is what everybody likes to see” and “creates so much positive trust” with investors. if (window.dfp_visibility === 'mobile' ) { googletag.cmd.push(function() { googletag.defineSlot( '/3618/biopharmadive/biopharmadivehybrid2', [[300, 250], 'fluid'], 'dfp-hybrid2-mobile' ).addService(googletag.pubads()); }); } waitToLoadAds.push(function() { googletag.cmd.push(function() { if (window.dfp_visibility === 'mobile' ) { window.onDvtagReady?.(() => googletag.display('dfp-hybrid2-mobile')); googletag.pubads().addEventListener('slotRenderEnded', function (event) { var adUnitPath = '/3618/biopharmadive/biopharmadivehybrid2'; var onProformative = false; if (onProformative && event.slot.getAdUnitPath() === adUnitPath && !event.isEmpty ) { var adUnitPathWithVisibility = adUnitPath + '-mobile'; var selector = '.pf-comments__ad-wrapper #dfp-hybrid2-mobile'; if (!$(selector).closest('.pf-comments__ad-wrapper').hasClass('borders')) { $(selector).closest('.pf-comments__ad-wrapper').addClass('borders') } } }); } }); }); Caribou checks some of the boxes that, according to deal experts, make for a good reverse merger candidate. It trades on the Nasdaq, for example, which is more attractive to private drug developers than lower-tier, over-the-counter markets. A researcher works in Caribou's labs, where the company was designing cell therapies for blood malignancies. Permission granted by Caribou Biosciences Caribou may also have a subzero enterprise value, which, in broad strokes, means that after accounting for its cash pile, the market is attributing nothing — or, really, less than nothing — to the company’s core operating business. That can actually be a plus to private developers, as it signals they might not have to pay a big premium to snag the public vehicle. Using its June 30 financials and closing share price Wednesday, Caribou would have a negative enterprise value of roughly $20 million. (Notably, that’s at the low end of a range from Leerink, which estimates the figure could be as much as $30 million depending on how much cash Caribou spent in the third quarter.) “I would definitely say a reverse merger is on the table here,” said Emmett Sweeney, a vice president on the healthcare investment banking team at Raymond James. Perhaps what makes Caribou such an obvious reverse merger prospect is it publicly stating that it’s exploring strategic alternatives. When companies do that, they become “low-hanging fruit” for reverse merger deals, according to David Kellman, a managing director and head of life sciences and biopharma investment banking at Citizens. They’re “basically running auction processes” with private companies, Kellman said in an interview earlier this month. “Those are the most obvious candidates, regardless of other criteria.” Caribou’s statement, including the mention of Wedbush being its strategic advisor, is a sign that company leaders are “serious” and “mean business,” Sweeney said. Clearly, “they want to move quickly. That's another aspect of Caribou that makes it an attractive merger partner.” Sweeney and others anticipate that Caribou, if not already, will soon be inundated with inbounds from private companies interested in merging. With roughly two dozen biotech reverse mergers announced this year, “the question for many companies is no longer whether the structure works, but whether they can find the right shell and execute the transaction on attractive terms,” Raymond James analysts wrote in a note to clients Wednesday. One lingering question is whether Caribou’s now-discontinued drugs will find a new home. Graybosch doesn’t have high hopes — in part because of rival programs advancing at other cell therapy developers like Fate Therapeutics and AvenCell Therapeutics, both of which are backed by major life sciences investors and large pharmaceutical firms. “Very rarely do these assets show up [again],” she said. “If I'm an investor thinking, ‘Do I wrap a new company around this asset, or do I go invest in AvenCell or Fate,’ I probably choose AvenCell or Fate at this point.” Recommended Reading A booming business on Wall Street would love more biotechs to quietly die By Jacob Bell • Sept. 10, 2026 Add us on Google Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Filed Under: Deals
